errors.description: Welt length, measured two ways. Against BUTTON SPACING - a landmark on the camera-facing placket and therefore not distorted by body rotation - the drawing's welt is 1.14 button-spacings and the render's 1.56, about 37 percent too long. Against half-chest width the drawing gives 0.39 and the render 0.46-0.55 depending where the occluded side seam falls. Both landmarks agree on direction and rough size, and because horizontal distances are foreshortened by body rotation while button spacing is not, 37 percent is a FLOOR not a ceiling.
errors.expected: Each chest welt about 1.14 button-spacings long, spanning roughly 0.39 of the half-chest width
errors.correction: Shorten each welt to about 1.14 button-spacings - a compact chest besom whose outer end finishes with a clear field of plain cloth between it and the armhole, roughly as wide again as the gap between its inner end and the front edge.

errors.description: Outboard position of the pair. In the drawing each welt sits closer to the front edge than to the side: inboard margin about 0.22-0.27 of half-chest, outboard about 0.37, welt centre about 0.42 of the way out. In the render the inner end is 1.04 button-spacings from the front edge against 0.65 drawn, and the outer end runs nearly into the armhole - outboard margin 0.08-0.23 against 0.37 drawn. The whole pair is displaced outboard by roughly a fifth of the half-chest. Corroborated independently: the front dart sits at 0.48 of half-chest in the drawing and 0.51-0.62 in the render, so the panel's whole internal geometry is pushed outboard.
errors.expected: Welt inner end about 0.65 button-spacings from the front edge, welt centre about 0.42 of the way to the side seam, outboard margin about 0.37 of half-chest
errors.actual: Inner end about 1.04 button-spacings out; outer end nearly touching the armhole
errors.correction: Slide both welts inboard so each begins about 0.65 button-spacings out from the front edge and ends with a broad expanse of plain cloth - a good third of the half-chest - between its outer end and the armhole seam.

errors.description: The option is 'Right & Left Besom', meaning two chest welts one per side. There ARE two - the count is correct - but the wearer's-right welt is SEVERED BY THE LEFT FRAME EDGE with only about a quarter of its length inside the picture. The single fact the image exists to teach, that these welts come as a mirrored pair, is not legible.
errors.expected: Two chest welts mirrored either side of the front edge, BOTH WHOLLY VISIBLE so the pairing is immediately readable, as the drawing shows them
errors.actual: Two welts at matching height, but the wearer's-right one cropped at the frame edge, reading as a stray dark mark rather than a pocket
errors.correction: Pull the camera back and centre the front edge in the frame so both chest welts sit complete inside the picture with the placket and its buttons running between them, the pair reading as an obvious mirrored set across the chest.

errors.description: Welt slant. In the drawing both welts tilt outboard-end-high at about 12-13 degrees. The render tilts the same way but at only about 3 degrees, reading almost horizontal.
errors.expected: About 12-13 degrees, outboard end high, mirrored on both sides
errors.correction: Lift the outboard end of each welt so it runs a clear 12 degrees uphill from the front edge toward the armhole, mirrored across the placket.

errors.description: Welt depth. The render's welt is a very fine dark slit with almost no lip depth, reading as a hairline jet. The drawing's red bars are heavy, but red marks POSITION not dimension, so no width figure is taken from them; the finding is only that a besom needs a legible lip and the render barely shows one.
errors.expected: A besom pocket with a defined welt lip framing the opening, no flap
errors.actual: A hairline slit with minimal lip and little tonal separation from the ground cloth
errors.correction: Build each welt with a visible lip of the same navy cloth about one third of a button diameter deep, its top face catching light and casting a fine shadow into the opening below, ends squared and pressed flat, with no flap.

notes:
Count is right; both previous faults persist and a new compositional one has appeared.

The measurement discipline here is worth keeping: welt length was checked against BUTTON SPACING rather than chest width, because button spacing lies on the camera-facing placket and is not compressed by body rotation, whereas half-chest width is. The two normalisations agree on direction, and the button-spacing figure (1.56 against 1.14) is the trustworthy one.

Where a number could not be pinned, a BRACKET was reported rather than a convenient point value: the wearer's-right side of the body is out of frame and the wearer's-left side seam is hidden behind the arm, so the body edge can only be bracketed, giving 0.46-0.55 rather than a single figure.

NOT measurable: absolute welt length or lip depth in centimetres (no dimension callouts, and the red bars mark position not thickness); symmetry between the two welts, since only one is fully in frame; anything below mid-chest on the wearer's right.

BLUEPRINT_CONFLICT is false: the drawing is unambiguously a waistcoat front - short shoulder straps, curved armholes, side seams, front darts, buttoned placket - and the render is a waistcoat.
